The '''P4''' is an unarmoured [[off-road vehicle]] used by the [[military of France]]. It was manufactured by [[Peugeot]] but is now manufactured by [[Panhard]]. It is to be replaced with the [[Petit Véhicule Protégé|PVP]] by Panhard. The P4 is a derivative of the [[Mercedes-Benz G-Class|Mercedes Geländewagen]] military version built under license by Peugeot for the [[Military of France|French military]]. Peugeot did not have a licence to export the vehicle anywhere else than to the countries bound to France by defence agreements.

== History ==
In the late 1960s, the French army decided that its 10,001 [[Hotchkiss M201|Jeeps]] needed to be replaced. The replacement vehicle would carry four men with radio equipment and would be small enough to be parachuted and transported by plane.

After many technical issues, the new vehicle was designed in the 1970s. Agreement was reached between Peugeot and Mercedes to co-produce the vehicle on a 50:50 basis. Peugeot installed the engine of the [[Peugeot 504]] and the [[Transmission (mechanics)|transmission]] of the [[Peugeot 604]] on the [[Mercedes-Benz G-Class]]; it also installed the electrical systems, welded the exterior and painted the car. The rest was done by Mercedes.  The plant in [[Sochaux]] did the final assembly. The first prototype was tested in 1978, beginning a long series of tests and trials, notably a rally in south [[Algeria]] with a petrol and a diesel P4.

The [[French Army]] ordered 15,000 P4s, both petrol and diesel versions; in 1981, the order was reduced to 13,500 units with the downsizing of the Army. From 1985, production was transferred to [[Panhard]] in [[Marolles-en-Hurepoix]], where 6,000 vehicles were produced. In 2016, P4s were donated to the Cameroonian military for its special forces units.<ref name="CAM">{{Cite web|url=http://www.defenceweb.co.za/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=46244:france-donates-military-equipment-to-cameroon&catid=50:Land&Itemid=105|title = France donates military equipment to Cameroon|date = 12 December 2016}}</ref>

A civilian version was made, but encountered little success because of the high price and a poor [[power-to-weight ratio]].

In 2016, the French military ordered 500 Technamm Masstech T4 VLTP VP vehicles as an interim replacement to the P4.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.joint-forces.com/features/16460-french-technamm-masstech-t4-vltp-vp|title = French Technamm Masstech T4 VLTP VP|date = 3 August 2018}}</ref>

===P4D===
In 1992, the Army converted around 1,300 petrol P4s into diesel P4D (''P4 Diesel'') models.<ref name="MT">{{Cite web |url=http://www.military-today.com/trucks/peugeot_p4.htm |title=Peugeot P4 Light utility vehicle |access-date=2021-10-03 |archive-date=2021-12-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223210343/http://www.military-today.com/trucks/peugeot_p4.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> The conversion was executed by Panhard (1300 VLTT) and the ''Établissements régionaux du matériel''. The engine, a 2.5-liter Peugeot four-cylinder, is the same as used in the original diesel P4.

===P4P===
The P4 P (''P4 Protégé'', "protected P4") is an armoured version,<ref name="MT"/> with 80 units built in the 1990s. An armored version was made at the request of Peugeot by CBH Institutions (Constructions Blindées of Hardricourt).

This version has been evaluated by the French Army and commissioned by the Navy for the Protection of sensitive sites. Five different versions were produced.

* P4 CBH AKIS 2400
* P4 CBH SUPER AKIS 2850
* P4 CBH 3120

The four digits at the end of the name signify the three wheelbases of {{convert|2400|,|2850|, or|3120|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} that were available. Some P4 armored CBH have been manufactured for use in [[Lebanon]].

An operation Manufacturer and the [[GIGN]] was conducted in November 1988 for testing rolling over 24 hours. The P4 Shielded CBH AKIS blue police carried out the range of 1000&nbsp;km to the average of 134.5&nbsp;km per hour and the total distance of 3180&nbsp;km in 24 hours is an average of 132.5&nbsp;km / hour with 4 men on board. The engine was a 2.5-litre turbo exchanger amended by CBH, which had an output of 150&nbsp;hp.

===P4 VPS===
[[File:French SF1 Domenjod 120618.jpg|thumb|A Panhard VPS in service with French special forces.]]

Version of the P4 for French special forces. Contract was awarded to Panhard by the DGA in 2005.<ref name="ARVPS">{{Cite web|url=https://www.armyrecognition.com/french_army_france_wheeled_armoured_vehicle_uk/vps_light_4x4_special_forces_patrol_vehicle_data_sheet_specifications_description_pictures_video.html|title=VPS 1 Light 4x4 Special Forces patrol vehicle data pictures video &#124; French army france wheeled armoured vehicle UK &#124; French army military equipment vehicle UK}}</ref> 51 VPSes were brought to service.<ref name="ARVPS"/>

They're equipped with armored floors to provide landmine protection.<ref name="ARVPS"/>

The VPS can be transported by either a C-160 Transall or C-130 Hercules.<ref name="ARVPS"/>

===P4 VIPAIR===
The P4 VIPAIR (Véhicule d'Intervention et de Projection Air – Air Intervention and Projection Vehicle) was created by Arquus in 2016,<ref name="ARQ">{{Cite web|url=https://www.arquus-defense.com/newsroom/news/arquus-delivers-last-vipair-p4-vehicle-french-air-and-space-force|title = Arquus delivers the last VIPAIR P4 vehicle to the French Air and Space Force &#124; Arquus}}</ref> which converted 19 P4 ASPICs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.edrmagazine.eu/delivery-of-the-last-vipair-p4-to-the-french-air-force |title = Arquus: the last VIPAIR P4 delivered to the French Air Force - EDR Magazine|date = 15 October 2020}}</ref>

The programme was completed on October 15, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.shephardmedia.com/news/landwarfareintl/arquus-completes-p4-vipair-deliveries/ |title = Arquus completes P4 VIPAIR deliveries - Shephard Media}}</ref>
